- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.03 to +0.37).  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.47 to -0.57) or after a recent peak — model tends to ignore downward momentum.  
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts often overshoot recent highs and undershoot recent lows, especially in the 10–20 day horizon.  
- When sentiment turns negative mid-period, model fails to adjust downward quickly — true price drops faster than forecasted.  
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses early price corrections and overreacts to sentiment shifts only after 3–5 days.  
- High sentiment volatility (e.g., +0.37 → -0.53) triggers model overcorrection — forecasts jump too far in either direction, then fail to stabilize.  
- Model underestimates downward trends when sentiment is negative but not extreme — e.g., -0.47 → -0.53, but price still drops 5–10% below forecast.  
- Avoid extrapolating recent sentiment trends into 30d — sentiment often reverses or weakens before true price action.  
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model tends to overestimate 30d price — especially if recent price is rising.  
- Model underestimates price drops after a spike if sentiment is negative but not extreme — e.g., -0.47 → -0.53, but price drops 10–15% below forecast.
